# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-28

**Your temple podcast went up with the title “What the Evidence Actually Say”, which names nothing people search: put Richard Eaton and the temples back in it today. The Churchill Short is due on 30 November with no script on disk, and the Sati Short, already written, takes the slot the lapsed Tegh Bahadur Short left.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish a Short for Churchill's birthday on 30 November: what his War Cabinet was told about the Bengal famine in 1943, and what it decided.** (short, due 2026-11-30, open since 2026-11-24)  
   Why: Two days left and no script on disk. A ruler convicted by his own papers is the channel's best shape for subscribers: “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History” brings 12.9 per 1,000 views, the best in the 90-day window. People search “winston churchill history” all year; that the birthday adds a lift is a guess.  
   First step: Write it today, record tomorrow, publish the morning of 30 November: a dated 1943 War Cabinet record in sentence one, no INA in the first 10 seconds. If it will not be recorded by tomorrow, drop it.
2. **Script and publish a follow-up long-form for the Indonesia video's viewers: why Bali stayed Hindu when Java converted.** (long, due 2026-12-02, open since 2026-11-19)  
   Why: The Indonesia long-form is the nearest breakout: short of the line of 500 net subscribers on 2026-11-25 but still adding them daily, at 3.9 per 1,000 views against the Asia video's 2. A follow-up reaches those viewers while they still come. Bali as the subject is a guess from the comments.  
   First step: Nothing is on disk and it is due in four days. Today pick the culprit and the dated act for sentence one and stay inside it for 30 seconds. Keep “Indonesia” in the title (see Competitors).
3. **Record and publish the Sati Short already written, for 4 December, the day in 1829 Bentinck outlawed sati: in those same years Englishmen sold their wives at market.** (short, due 2026-12-04, new)  
   Why: The only dated Short this week already written and sourced. Its shape, a British claim about Hindus turned back on Britain, is the shape of “Did Hindu mothers REALLY feed their babies to crocodiles?”, one of the channel's five best Shorts for subscribers per view. The earlier “How Missionaries Turned Sati Into a Fundraiser” earned little, so the lift is a guess.  
   First step: Fix the line the script flags (“never wrote a law”: courts did act under other charges), open on the date 4 December 1829, record by 2 December, publish the morning of 4 December.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
18,500 subscribers, up 500 in a week, against 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 21,078, which needs 88.3 net a day; the last 7 days ran at 75.3, below that pace, and the channel is 2,387 behind the ramp, so on the 7-day rate November ends near 18,651, 2,427 short. Furthest behind is breakouts: none this month against 2,071 subscribers planned from them, and breakouts carry 63.5% of lifetime subscribers. The Tegh Bahadur Short lapsed today with nothing made, the second dated Short to lapse in five days. Last week both uploads were your own picks and none of the brief's suggestions shipped, so this week's three are the two still open and one Short that is already written.

What's working
- “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” is this month's best subscriber-earner: 3.9 net per 1,000 views on 127,500 views, and long-form views rose 24.8% week over week. Long-form was 4 of the 23 uploads in the last 30 days, yet over 28 days it earned 87.7% of the net subscribers videos brought.
- The best subscriber-earner of the last 90 days is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, 12.9 net per 1,000 views, and over the 365-day window it is “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps”, 34.3. Both put a colonial-era culprit on trial with its own records. The Churchill and Sati Shorts are built the same way.
- The podcast's first day: 4,751 views in 27 hours, and the most-liked comments ask for more like it. Day one is the subscriber test; judge it on 30 November by engaged views and subscribers.

What's wrong
- Since yesterday the podcast's title went from “Did Hindus Kings Loot Temples?” to “What the Evidence Actually Say”: no question, no name, and a missing s. Long-form is found on Home (270,430 long-form views over 28 days came through Home and the subscriptions feed, against 7,957 from search), where the title is most of what a viewer sees. Probable cause of a slow second day, if it comes: nobody can tell what it is about. Test: retitle today and compare views an hour on 30 November with today's 174.6.
- Shorts views fell 63.9% week over week (19,524 against 54,051), and the three newest with data brought next to no subscribers: 0, 1.1 and 0 per 1,000 views. Probable cause: the Ramayana film Shorts have aged, and none of the newer ones rode a date or a release. Test: the Churchill and Sati Shorts each ride a date; judge both on day three against these three.
- Two dated Shorts lapsed in five days with nothing made, and neither open decision has a script on disk. Probable cause: dated Shorts are being chosen with less time than writing, recording and editing take. Test: if the Sati Short, written since September, ships on 4 December and the unwritten Churchill one does not, choose dated Shorts only from scripts already on disk a week ahead.
- Long-form views overstate real viewing: only 41.5% of November's long-form views were engaged views, and over the 365-day window long-form now brings 7.1 subscribers per 1,000 views, below the range it used to hold. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing, which YouTube has counted as views since August. Test: judge the podcast and the Bali video by engaged views and subscribers, never by views.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-25. Shorts are found in the Shorts feed: 147,158 Shorts views over 28 days came from it, against 83,137 from search. Outside YouTube, WhatsApp sends the most viewers: 13,102 views over the 365-day window, 28.1x what Instagram sends.
- Every objection under the podcast so far is about its theology: the opening line about the “only true path”, the Quran and the hadith (“you need to understand the context”). None of the top comments disputes an inscription. The Shorts cut from it should come from the inscription chapters.
- A Malaysian viewer adds that European colonisation “actually helped expedite the locals' conversion to Islam”, and an Indonesian Muslim viewer places the Allah-and-Ravana version in the Malay literary tradition. The Bali script should check both before it names a culprit.
- Indonesians are still correcting the Indonesia video in its comments, so the Bali video will be watched by people who know the ground. One wrong date there will be the top comment.

## How they are reacting
The week's comments are still mostly on the Indonesia long-form; the podcast's first comments bring praise for the format and objections to its theology.
- **Asking for more podcasts** (positive): "Bro please do more podcast like this ❤"
- **Muslim viewers contesting the podcast's theology** (negative): "Ok guys this is just hate many of the pints are wrong"
- **Southeast Asian viewers adding to the Indonesia video** (mixed): "A Malaysian here. This is true, but only part of the whole story."
- **Anger turning on Islam as a whole** (negative): "Everytime I learn more about Islam, it sounds like Sauron levels of evil maipulation"
- **The Ramayana as India's reach abroad** (positive): "It is our softpower"
- **Colonial Shorts read as being about today** (mixed): "Now the same people refuse to take Indian names, and instead take Bible names"

Requested topics
- More long conversations like the temple podcast
- Rajendra Chola's raid on Srivijaya
- Shri Krishna in the shape of the Asia Ramayana video
- Hindi versions of the long-forms

## Competitors
The watchlist is still riding the Ramayana film, on channels far larger than Itiha. The useful lessons this week are an opening line, a small channel's jump, and a naming clash.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Boycott the Ramayana? What?"
  Why it worked: 111,920 views at 21.4x the channel's usual. It opens on what the viewer is planning and says it is a mistake: “If you plan on boycotting the new Ramayan movie, you might be doing more harm than good. Let me explain.”
  Steal: For the Sati Short: open on what every viewer was taught, that Britain banned sati to save Indian women, and break it in the next sentence.
- **The History Of Bangalore**: "Purniah: The Man Who Loved Mysore More"
  Why it worked: 3,587 views at 11.9x its usual, on a channel of a few thousand subscribers. Purniah ran Mysore's government under Tipu Sultan and stayed on under the British; it went up the week Tipu was back in the news over the Latur row. That the news lifted it is a guess.
  Steal: When a ruler is in the news, the person who served beside him is the untold story, and a small channel can be found on it.
- **The Sham Sharma Show**: "Bali Death Dark Truth"
  Why it worked: 616,810 views at 4.2x its usual, one of that channel's run of Ramayana Shorts this month, so almost certainly about the Ramayana's Bali, not the island.
  Steal: A warning more than a lesson: “Bali” alone in a title now competes with the Ramayana's Bali. Keep “Indonesia” in the Bali video's title.

Gaps
- The Emissary's Short “What do Hindus Think of the Abrahamic God?” ran far above that channel's usual and nothing on Itiha answers it. The podcast's chapter at 5:05 covers the same ground, but it is the chapter viewers dispute, so it needs its sources on screen before it is clipped.
- The Emissary's “Why Did Japan Make Indian Propaganda Posters?” is the watchlist's best-scoring gap this month with nothing like it on Itiha. It has no culprit who wronged Indians, so it is a gap, not a pick.

## Trending now, make this
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: 14 December 1971: the killing of Bengal's intellectuals  
  Signal: Sixteen days out; the research step falls on 30 November and nothing is scripted. The channel's 1971 Short “1971 War: Operation Cactus Lily | Meghna Heli Bridge” is one of its five best Shorts for subscribers per view. (Calendar, own Shorts)  
  Make: On 30 November find who drew up the list and who carried it out, with names and the date. Script a Short of about two minutes for the morning of 14 December, the culprit in sentence one, and judge it on day three.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: 6 December: the Vishnu-Hari slab from the Babri rubble  
  Signal: Eight days out. Your second Irfan Habib Short, on the slab that came out of the rubble on 6 December 1992 and the museum stone he said it was, is written and waiting for your edit. (Calendar, script on disk)  
  Make: Edit it this week and record it in the same sitting as the Sati Short. Publish the morning of 6 December with “Vishnu Hari inscription” in the title, the searched name, and pin links between it and the first Habib Short. The first one earned little, so the date's lift is a guess.
- **watch, short, 3/5**: Timur's sack of Delhi, 17 December 1398  
  Signal: Nineteen days out; the research step falls on 3 December. (Calendar)  
  Make: From 3 December, check what Timur's own memoir says about the prisoners killed before the battle. If it holds, a Short for the morning of 17 December that opens on his words. The channel's earlier Timur Short brought no subscribers, so this is a guess.
- **watch, skip, 0/5**: Three films on 4 December: Maatrubhumi, Eetha, Baba  
  Signal: All three open on 4 December. The radar finds no confirmed history subject for any of them, and Baba's subject is unverified. (Film releases)  
  Make: Skip unless a trailer shows one is about a figure in the channel's lane. Do not script from headlines.
- **watch, skip, 1/5**: Guru Nanak  
  Signal: Guru Nanak's English Wikipedia readership is 8.05x its usual, 9,365 a day. (Wikipedia)  
  Make: Skip. A saint's life is one of the kinds of Short the channel's own checks turn down, and this week has three dated Shorts already.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [3/5, short] **Why Muhammad bin Qasim Kept Multan's Sun Idol Standing**  
  Extraction mechanism: by Alberuni's account the conqueror kept the idol because the pilgrims' offerings made Multan rich; Villain plus hypocrisy: in the same account he hung a piece of cow's flesh on its neck to mock it; Religion stakes: the first Arab conquest in India, in the eighth century  
  source: Already recorded: the podcast's chapter at 37:38, with Sachau's Alberuni on screen. Read the passage again before cutting it.
- [2/5, short] **The Inscription Richard Eaton Left Out: Vikramaditya II at Kanchi**  
  Contested history: answers the claim that Hindu kings looted each other's temples with the king's own inscription in the Kailasanatha temple (Epigraphia Indica, vol. III); Identity and religion stakes: who destroyed temples is the argument under every temple video  
  source: Already recorded: the podcast's chapter at 34:56. Set the Short's Related video to the podcast; whether a clip sends viewers on is a guess.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,559 followers, up only 12 in the last 7 days, 1.7 a day. The newest reel, on Richard Eaton's temple claim, reached 1,799 on its first day with a skip rate of 38.9%, better than the reel median of 53.7%. November's feed posts cannot be judged yet, because their follows keep arriving for about three weeks.

Do more
- Write carousels that correct the record  
  51 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53 followers against 21 for the other lanes (41 posts). Median reach 15.3k vs 11.0k, conversion 3.77 vs 1.97 per 1k. 464 followers a month at stake.
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 34.5 followers (92 posts); outside the band, 12 (16 posts). Pooled rate 2.89 vs 1.85 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 411 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  18 of 104 rated posts are shared above the median (24.7/1k) but convert below it (2.1/1k): median 9.8k reach for a median 9 followers. The 34 posts that do both average 278 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 946 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  88 single images all time: 87.9k reach between them and 125 followers, 1.4 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 156.5. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 90 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **now**: Retitle the podcast. “What the Evidence Actually Say” could read “Did Hindu Kings Loot Temples? Richard Eaton vs the Inscriptions”.  
  Its own description opens with that question and names Eaton, and those are the words a searcher types. It has 4,751 views so far, so few have seen the current title.
- **this_week**: Set the Related video of today's Short, “Richard Eaton Says Hindu Kings DESTROYED Temples”, to the podcast, and pin the podcast's link in its comments.  
  The Short is the podcast's way in. Whether a Short sends viewers on is a guess, but the link takes a minute.
- **this_week**: Upload the Malay Ravana Short to YouTube with its Related video set to the Indonesia long-form.  
  Written since 19 November and still not on YouTube, while the Indonesia long-form keeps bringing subscribers every day.
- **this_week**: Answer the theology objections under the podcast with sources (/replies drafts them).  
  They are the only disputes so far; answered, they protect the inscription chapters the Shorts will be cut from.
- **later**: Set GA4_PROPERTY_ID in .env.  
  Without it the brief cannot read itiha.info; Search Console shows only searches for the name “itiha”.
